intro: Essays, papers and lab write-ups on AI security, detection and threat intelligence. Each piece is labelled with what it is: an argument (Essay, Paper, Note) or something built and tested (Lab, Project).

tracks.name: AI Security
tracks.blurb: Securing agents and the systems they run in: isolation, identity, injection and poisoning.

tracks.name: Detection & Response
tracks.blurb: Detection engineering, deception and response, measured against how intrusions actually move.

tracks.name: Threat Intelligence
tracks.blurb: What CTI keeps, and what it hands off, when offensive capability stops varying between actors.

future-of-cti.title: The Future of CTI: A Forecast
future-of-cti.summary: When capability stops varying between attackers, an attacker's means track the target's exposure, and predicting techniques from actor history loses most of its value for prevention. An intelligence estimate on what that does to threat intelligence: what hands off to other teams, what stays, and what to build now.

detection-priority.title: After the Heat Map: Prioritizing Detections When Any Technique Is Possible
detection-priority.summary: Ranking detections when actor history stops predicting technique: a filter chain built on paths to critical assets, coverage measured as the share of paths cut by validated detections, and a staged transition from actor-weighted coverage.

cti-as-code.title: CTI as Code: The Intelligence Program as Version-Controlled Records
cti-as-code.summary: The threat intelligence program itself, held as version-controlled records whose claims about each other are enforced in CI. Every intelligence question resolves to a collection source or names a gap, or the build fails. Agents declare a contract before they may run, and an agent that reads adversary-written text may not run unattended.

agent-first-tip.title: Agent-First TIP
agent-first-tip.summary: A threat intelligence platform built on first-party evidence, where agents propose, gates check, and humans own ground truth.

agentic-iam.title: Agentic IAM: Designing Blast Radius for AI Agents
agentic-iam.summary: Access control for AI agents across issuance, delegation, execution and monitoring: just-in-time credentials, model-proposed scopes bounded by a human-authored ceiling, capability tokens with provably attenuated delegation, and attested agent identity. Framed as falsifiable hypotheses.

agentic-tarpit.title: Tarpitting Agentic Attacks
agentic-tarpit.summary: Research into deception for agentic attackers. A maintained catalog of agent weaknesses is turned against an attacker inside our own environment, to stall it, misdirect it and make it reveal itself, measured by attacker time to objective. Our own agents and staff must be able to tell real from decoy by construction. Pre-prototype; no experiment has run.

most-ai-security-is-security.title: Most AI Security Is Security
most-ai-security-is-security.summary: Comparing the ways organizations control coding agents, the controls that reached every agent were endpoint management, network egress and identity, none of them built for AI. Most of the risk in an AI system comes down to questions security programs already know how to answer, and the AI-specific tools belong on top, for the residue.

the-workload-is-the-adversary.title: The Workload Is the Adversary: Isolation for AI Systems When the Thing Inside Is Hostile
the-workload-is-the-adversary.summary: Most security architecture assumes the workload is on your side. AI puts a possible adversary inside the boundary: agents following injected instructions, training jobs on unread data, tenants on shared accelerators. Nine falsifiable hypotheses and a layer-by-layer reference architecture, from a coding agent in CI up to a training cluster holding model weights. Nothing built yet; a lab is testing the first four.
